page: Amazon Web Services m7i.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8488C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, providing dedicated CPU allocation. It includes 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, which equates to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache specifications include 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 105 MB L3 cache. There is no local storage or GPU bundled with this instance, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities but limited multi-core scaling due to the dual-vCPU configuration. Single-core tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, place the instance in the average middle tier. However, multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, and ray tracing benchmarks fall into the bottom 10% to 25% categories. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached and uncached operations show weak to poor throughput. Similarly, database operations, Redis SET performance, and static web serving throughput are positioned in the lower performance tiers. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for integer and vector operations, though overall LLM inference speeds remain low.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m7i.large offers a low-cost entry point into dedicated Intel Xeon Sapphire Rapids generation hardware without the variable performance risks of burstable instances. The tradeoff is its low absolute resource density, particularly in multi-threaded scenarios and memory-intensive operations. This instance is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, small-scale text processing, single-threaded applications, and development or testing environments that require dedicated CPU execution but do not demand high memory bandwidth or local storage.
